title: Green beans, canned, reduced sodium, cooked with oil

content.title: About
content.content: Canned green beans that are prepared with reduced sodium and cooked in vegetable oil provide a ready‑to‑eat vegetable side. The beans retain most of their nutrients, and the added oil enhances flavor and aids absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green beans are a good source of fiber, B‑vitamins, and vitamin C.
Reduced‑sodium canning helps lower the risk of high blood pressure.
Cooking in oil preserves aroma and makes the beans more satisfying.
Canned beans have a long shelf life without refrigeration.
They are a convenient fresh‑vegetable alternative during winter months.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity and participates in collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Reduced sodium
items.content: Lower salt content helps manage blood pressure.

items.title: Fat‑soluble vitamins from oil
items.content: The added oil aids absorption of vitamins A, D, E and K.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Even reduced‑sodium products still contain salt; people with hypertension should monitor total intake.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to beans.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Certain brands may use additives such as benzoates; check labels if you are sensitive.

items.title: Caloric contribution from oil
items.content: Oil adds calories, so portion size should be considered in calorie‑controlled diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Green beans can be eaten cold in salads, warmed in the microwave or skillet, added to soups, stews, and casseroles. They pair well with garlic, lemon, herbs, and lean proteins such as chicken or fish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened can in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer beans to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for up to 5‑7 days. Discard if an off‑odor or discoloration appears.
